summary: How AML/CFT supervisors, FIUs, prudential authorities and AMLA cooperate across borders through colleges and information exchange, and how AML/CFT controls interact with EU restrictive measures and targeted financial sanctions.
topic: Reducing Financial Crime & Delivering Market Integrity
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How AML/CFT supervisors, FIUs, prudential authorities and AMLA cooperate across borders through colleges and information exchange, and how AML/CFT controls interact with EU restrictive measures and targeted financial sanctions.
Learning Objectives: Operate AML/CFT supervisory colleges and home–host cooperation effectively
Coordinate AML/CFT findings with prudential supervisors, FIUs and resolution authorities
Assess how firms integrate targeted financial sanctions into AML/CFT controls
Syllabus: AML/CFT colleges, information exchange and cooperation with prudential supervisors
AML/CFT considerations in authorisation, qualifying holdings and withdrawal
Targeted financial sanctions and screening obligations under the AML Regulation
Sanctions evasion typologies and criminal enforcement of restrictive measures
Intended Audience: AML/CFT supervisors, inspectors and policy staff at national competent authorities and self-regulatory bodies
MLROs, compliance officers, financial crime risk and legal staff at credit institutions, financial institutions and crypto-asset service providers
Senior managers and management body members accountable for the AML/CFT framework and transition planning
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of AML/CFT compliance or supervision is helpful. No legal background or prior knowledge of EU law is required.
Core Reading: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 on the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purposes of money laundering or terrorist financing (AML Regulation)

Directive (EU) 2024/1640 on the mechanisms to be put in place by Member States for the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purposes of money laundering or terrorist financing (AMLD6)
Regulation (EU) 2024/1620 establishing the Authority for Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AMLA Regulation)
Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 on information accompanying transfers of funds and certain crypto-assets (Transfer of Funds Regulation)
